title: Example 13-3: Three-Level Poem

illustrates.quote: The indention pattern is based on the entire poem. The main entry begins in cell 1. Each subentry level begins two cells to the right of the previous level. All runovers begin two cells to the right of the farthest indented level. One level: 1-3 Two levels: 1-5, 3-5 Three levels: 1-7, 3-7, 5-7 Four levels: 1-9, 3-9, 5-9, 7-9 etc.

blocks.features: Untitled excerpt (opening of Gerard Manley Hopkins's "Pied Beauty"); print shows three visually staggered indention levels among the six lines.

lines.text: Glory be to God for dappled things—
For skies of couple-colour as a brinded cow;
For rose-moles all in stipple upon trout that swim;
Landscape plotted and pieced—fold, fallow, and plough;
And all trades, their gear and tackle and trim.
